evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Not delivered. Rep jumped directly into probing without time-boxing the call or framing the dependable quote promise.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing had started: 'Well, so let's knock about the move aside from the pricing. Trevor. Do you have any concerns about the moving process?' This came after pickup address and square footage were already confirmed.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer said 'No, not particularly I think it'll be pretty smooth.' No concern raised, so no follow-up gap.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Full — property type (apartment), floor (second floor stairs only), rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (20 feet from parking to stairs, 10 feet from stairs to unit), special considerations (no elevator, reserved parking spot), destination floor (first floor), destination parking (immediate, unreserved).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. No recognizable version of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked and confirmed: 'normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?' Customer: 'Yes, that sounds accurate.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — rep gave typical range for one-bedroom apartment (2.5–3.5 hours) and personalized it to second-floor-to-first-floor specifics: 'in your case, we're only coming from a second floor to a first floor apartment. So I estimate the move to finish in two and a half to three and a half hours.' Estimate: '$520 to $728.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — transparency on hourly rate ($104/mover, $208 for two), what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wraps, pads, tools), explicit statement of no hidden fees ('no hidden fees of any type'), and 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute increments: 'We have a two and a half hour minimum and once we go over the minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moved directly from estimate to scheduling without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or waiting for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not delivered. No mention of on-time guarantee or discount terms.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not delivered. No mention of No Worries Damage Coverage or $2,000 coverage.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — neither of the two promises was delivered, so there was nothing to close the loop on.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep never returned to check what was still concerning Trevor after the estimate was given.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was delivered.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out — rep offered booking but gave a soft exit: 'if something comes up, if ever you want to reschedule or cancel, no fees for that. So would you like to be on the schedule today?' Customer indicated he was waiting on other quotes and wanted to call back later. Rep accepted this without a hard close: 'yes, of course. I can just also send you the estimate details to your email... And then I'll send this to TV on 99 @gmail.com.' This is a built-in out, not a clear 'Would you like our help with your move?' framed as a genuine ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Mentioned — 'No deposit is required. So, if something comes up, if ever you want to reschedule or cancel, no fees for that.' This covers no-deposit/rate-lock adjacent language.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — arrival window negotiated and tentatively confirmed (11:00 AM to 1:00 PM, later adjusted to 9:00 AM to 9:30 AM as maximum flexibility), date confirmed (September 30th), email sent. Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size confirmation, delivery address re-confirmed in booking context, and notes for crew about customer's concerns (though there were none to note).

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details with precision and follow-up questions (distances, floor levels, parking, special items, appliances) that created a solid foundation for the estimate, and she provided transparent pricing with clear rate breakdown and fee disclosures.
coaching_note: Open with the quid-pro-quo framing (10–15 minutes + dependable quote + wait for yes) before jumping into probing, skip the Two Promises entirely (both On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage were never mentioned), and ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate, then pause—do not fill the silence.
booking_note: Trevor explicitly stated he's 'waiting on quotes from a couple of other vendors' and asked to call back later, indicating no commitment was made on this call.
